title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether integrating a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier (with at most one automated repair) increases the fraction of intent‑driven configuration proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic NetOps validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Each pair evaluated a single shared_initial candidate under two conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (deterministic validation and ≤1 automated repair). Results: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); paired contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and model, single‑shot generation was near ceiling, limiting observable marginal rescue by the guarded pipeline. All preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts are archived with the study id to support replication and follow‑up experiments that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, or repair budget.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to network operations (NetOps) tasks such as intent→configuration translation, template synthesis, and automated repair. Operators require semantic guarantees—sequencing, reachability, and policy preservation—that cannot be assessed by syntax alone. Consequently, hybrid architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded automated repair (generate→validate→repair) have been proposed to reduce operational risk. However, the practical benefit of such architectures depends on how the estimand is defined (what is held fixed), the generator's single-shot quality, the validator's expressiveness, and the allowed repair budget.

We preregistered a paired experiment (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) that isolates the deterministic rescue utility of a validator and limited repair on the same LLM candidate. For each intent we generated one shared_initial candidate using gpt-5-mini and compared two treatments applied to that identical candidate: baseline (accept the single candidate without repair) and guarded (run deterministic validation and allow at most one automated repair). The research question: does adding a deterministic verifier plus at most one automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting the same single candidate without repair? Our contributions are (1) a preregistered paired evaluation (N=300 pairs) conditioned on shared_initial candidates that isolates deterministic rescue utility; (2) a fully archived execution and analysis bundle including deterministic validator traces and the single repaired episode; and (3) an empirical interpretation of estimator conditioning, ceiling effects, and operational implications for NetOps pipelines.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and systems work document extensive activity at the intersection of LLMs and NetOps, covering intent‑based translation, configuration synthesis, repair, and tool‑augmented agentic frameworks. Several studies describe generate→validate→repair architectures and planner‑centric tool orchestration that call external validators to improve correctness [doi:10.1609/aaai.v40i40.40676; https://openalex.org/W4389518608]. Empirical reports show that validator‑assisted generation often reduces errors, but absolute success rates vary with dataset, task difficulty, and validator coverage [https://openalex.org/W4416927413; https://openalex.org/W4404240614]. Surveys note practitioner skepticism about deployability even when syntactic correctness is high [https://openalex.org/W7167855398; https://openalex.org/W4416927413].

Two methodological gaps motivated our design. First, many prior comparisons conflate validator rescue with benefits from drawing additional independent model candidates: allowing resampling or iterative generation can increase success but mixes estimator effects. Second, standardized public benchmarks emphasizing semantic correctness (reachability, policy compliance) remain limited. We position our experiment to address the first gap by conditioning on a single shared_initial candidate per intent, thereby quantifying only the deterministic recovery achievable without additional independent model draws.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered study cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001 and froze the primary estimand: the absolute paired difference in the unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded minus baseline) computed on paired cases evaluating the same shared_initial candidate. The preregistration specified design, inclusion/exclusion rules, analysis executor, multiplicity plan, contamination controls, and reproducible executor inputs.

Task generation and difficulty strata. Tasks were generated deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 into a synthetic_topology_suite_v1 and stratified by generator metadata into low/medium/high difficulty (100 tasks per stratum). Difficulty metadata included changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, and required_command_count. Representative intent patterns: "shutdown_configure_restore" (medium) and "paired_link_atomic_mtu_change" (hard). The task manifest and six representative task responses are archived in the run bundle.

Modeling and orchestration. The declared model was gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). To isolate deterministic rescue of the same model output, the pipeline produced a single shared_initial generation per pair. The guarded condition reuses that candidate, runs the deterministic validator, and—if flagged—permits at most one automated repair attempt before a final deterministic revalidation. The baseline condition accepts the same shared_initial candidate unmodified.

Validator, scoring rule, and repair policy. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) implements the preregistered full_intent_constraint_validation rule: deterministic checks for sequencing constraints (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), preserved unspecified state, required_command_count, reachability invariants embedded in the synthetic topology, and forbidden-template protections (protected_interfaces). Scoring is binary per the preregistered rule: unflagged == pass; flagged after allowed repair == failure. The guarded repair policy allowed a single automated repair invocation (repair budget ≤1) that attempted a localized corrective edit to the shared_initial candidate; repair provider traces and validator rechecks are recorded for forensic inspection.

Design accounting, pilot, and stopping. The preregistration included an optional pilot (n = 60) for estimating discordance and calibrating power; that pilot was not executed and no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed. Confirmatory main run: planned_episode_count = 600 (300 pairs × 2 conditions), maximum_model_calls = 600, stopping rule required 300 analyzable pairs after exclusions. Exclusion rules allow pair exclusion only when both calls fail due to provider/infrastructure outages; per preregistered missingness handling, single-call failures are retained and treated per the executor. All such rules are recorded in the preregistration artifact.

Analysis executor and inference. The preregistered analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1: compute contingency counts n11, n10, n01, n00; report absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline), an exact two‑sided McNemar equivalent p‑value, and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI using bootstrap_seed = 1729 and B = 10000 resamples. Sensitivity analyses and subgroup strata were marked exploratory with Benjamini–Hochberg correction when applied. All analysis code, seeds, and executor inputs were frozen and archived.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter completed the confirmatory run (execution manifest): completed_episode_count = 600, complete_pair_count = 300, and model_calls_used = 301 (300 shared_initial + 1 repair). Deterministic reconciliation recorded stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 300, repair: 1} and cache_miss_count = 301. No provider outages, failed episodes, or unscorable episodes were recorded (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). The contamination summary is empty.

Marginal and paired outcomes. Marginal condition summary (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline successes = 299/300 (0.9966666667), guarded successes = 300/300 (1.0). The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 299, n10 = 1 (guarded‑only), n01 = 0 (baseline‑only), n00 = 0. The preregistered confirmatory analysis produced absolute paired difference = 0.0033333333333332993, exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0, and 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Per‑stratum outcomes: low = 100/100 baseline & guarded; medium = 100/100 baseline & guarded; high = baseline 99/100 vs guarded 100/100.

Rescue diagnostic. The single discordant episode (n10 = 1) invoked the permitted automated repair (repair stage_count = 1). The validator trace attributes the initial flag to a sequencing omission: the shared_initial candidate omitted a required 'admin down' prior to a VLAN/MTU change (must_be_down_for_fields violation). The automated repair inserted the missing sequencing command and the validator subsequently returned valid == true. The low‑level repair provider trace and full validator trace are archived; here we report the concise semantic summary of the corrected sequencing omission.

Statistical interpretation. With baseline single‑shot success near ceiling (299/300), the number of discordant pairs (m = n10 + n01 = 1) controls inference sensitivity rather than total N. The exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0 reflects the paucity of discordant evidence under the shared_initial estimand; the paired bootstrap CI bounds the plausible absolute paired improvement in this experimental context at ≤1 percentage point. These results do not imply equivalence of strategies under different estimand choices (e.g., allowing resampling) or on different task distributions.
sections.discussion:
Estimator conditioning and operational meaning. The shared_initial estimand intentionally conditions on a single LLM draw per intent and therefore measures only deterministic validator/repair rescue applied to that single candidate. This corresponds to operational workflows where a single model call is the normative procedure and the organization applies deterministic auditing and bounded automatic repair before deployment. It excludes verifier benefits attainable by independent alternative LLM draws per condition (resampling, iterative candidate generation, or verifier‑guided steering), which operational pipelines may permit and which could yield larger marginal improvements.

Ceiling effect and power considerations. The preregistered power target (detecting a 0.10 absolute paired improvement at two‑sided α = 0.05 with ≈0.8 power) assumed appreciable baseline discordance. The observed baseline of 299/300 produced only one discordant pair and thus limited inferential sensitivity for small absolute effects. The optional pilot (n = 60) for discordance estimation described in the preregistration was not executed; had it been run and reported low discordance, the preregistration allowed amendment before the main run. Practitioners designing similar confirmatory tests should run a small pilot to estimate discordance under their sampling frame and adjust sample size or estimand accordingly.

Validator coverage and sample representativeness. The deterministic validator checks sequencing, preservation of unspecified state, required_command_count, reachability invariants encoded in the synthetic topology, and forbidden-template protections. In our synthetic suite the dominant observed failure mode was sequencing omission; other failure classes that the validator could detect (reachability violations or forbidden-template modifications) were not observed at scale. This distribution of failures is a property of the deterministic task generator and the chosen difficulty stratification; real operational distributions might trigger different failure-mode mixes and change the marginal value of guarded pipelines.

Operational recommendations. When integrating a validator/repair scaffold, explicitly map the production workflow to the estimand under evaluation: if operations rely on a single model call, the shared_initial analysis here is relevant and shows deterministic audit+bounded repair can correct localized sequencing omissions. If an organization permits multiple candidate draws, resampling or verifier‑guided selection should be evaluated as a separate estimand because it can materially increase rescue opportunities. If higher marginal safety is required, consider expanding the repair budget (iterative repairs), allowing resampling, or using stronger domain‑tuned generation models.

Reproducibility and artifact grounding. All preregistration documents, task manifests, model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json), raw responses, provider traces, validator traces, analysis CSVs (analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/missingness_summary.csv), deterministic reconciliation, and analysis logs (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) are archived under the study id in the run bundle. The analysis parameters (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729) and the exact executor outputs are recorded. Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode accounting and provider call audit counts; these artifacts permit independent re‑execution of the confirmatory calculations by another deterministic executor.

Limitations and threats to validity. Internal validity: the shared_initial design isolates deterministic repair but does not measure benefits from alternative generation strategies. Construct validity: the binary unflagged/flagged outcome depends on validator expressiveness—semantic safety measured here is limited to the validator's encoded invariants. External validity: single model (gpt-5-mini), synthetic topology suite, and deterministic task generator constrain generalization to different LLMs, production topologies, or operator incident distributions. Conclusion validity: near‑ceiling baseline limited discordant observations and therefore statistical sensitivity to small absolute improvements. These limitations are discussed explicitly in the preregistration and are reflected in the released artifacts.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired comparison between a verifier‑assisted pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair) and accepting a single‑shot LLM candidate under the shared_initial estimand on 300 synthetic NetOps intents using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Baseline single‑shot generation produced 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300, yielding an absolute paired improvement of 0.00333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). The near‑ceiling baseline limits inferential sensitivity for small absolute improvements under the shared_initial estimand. We release the preregistration id, execution and analysis artifacts, representative task manifests, and validator traces in the archived run bundle to enable reproducible follow‑ups that vary estimand choice, model strength, or repair strategies.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre‑specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition.
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
